title: eight type-only wrappers around a layer or around a capability argument leave the layer resolvable, so Layer.provide still subtracts what it provides and the program runs
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Layer Algebra': 'A layer MUST associate each capability's nominal context key with a compatible service instance. Layer APIs are library-shaped; the compiler recognizes their effect on R without introducing special provider grammar.' and 'Satisfaction': 'Providing a layer to a computation MUST remove matching capabilities from the computation's unsatisfied requirement row.' A `satisfies`, an `as`, an angle-bracket assertion and a parenthesis are TYPE-only: they are erased before anything runs and the operand is the same `Layer.succeed(...)` call it was without them. So the closure is still known, the subtraction must still happen, and the program must still run. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS AND WHY IT IS ONE CASE WITH EIGHT SPELLINGS: on 2026-08-27 the Go fork's layer resolver was found to fail open under exactly these wrappers, and closing it moved 143 divergent cells while conformance reported 0 divergent throughout — because NO corpus case exercised a layer under a type-only wrapper at all. That is the gap this case closes, and it is written as one program with eight wrappers for the same reason `05-context-rows/sound-capability-receivers-keep-their-row-and-run` is: the failure guarded against is one over-correction, not eight. A resolver that starts stripping wrappers can very easily start stripping expressions that are NOT type-only, and this repository has shipped seven over-corrections. Each spelling targets a distinct mechanism, so a fix that over- or under-fires anywhere turns THIS case red rather than passing quietly: `satisfies` and `as` on the argument (the two the fork accepted while resolving nothing); an angle-bracket assertion (the same node kind as `as` reached through different syntax); `as unknown as` (two hops, so a resolver that strips one level and stops is caught); the wrapper on a `const` INITIALIZER rather than on the argument, which requires following the binding and THEN stripping rather than the other way round; a wrapped operand of `Layer.merge`, which is the composition path rather than the provide path and needs a second capability to be visible at run time; and two wrappers on the CAPABILITY argument of `Layer.succeed` rather than on the layer — a parenthesis and a `satisfies` — which is a different table on both backends and closed a pre-existing divergence in the opposite direction, the reference having refused `Layer.succeed((Directory), directory)` that the fork always accepted. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the requirement row itself. No corpus expectation can read a row; what it can observe is that a single `Layer.succeed(Directory, directory)` subtracts every one of these, which is the observable form of the same statement. It also does not pin a non-null assertion (`!`), which is NOT type-only in the relevant sense and must stay opaque — that is `a-non-null-assertion-is-not-a-type-only-wrapper`, deliberately a separate case so that this one's green never depends on `!` being in or out of the table. WHY THE OUTPUT IS NOT EIGHT IDENTICAL LINES: three of the eight look up 'zoe' rather than 'ada' and one is stamped by a second capability, so the printed lines are `Ada`, `none` and `Ada@7` in a fixed order. A resolver that quietly reordered, dropped or duplicated a provide scope would produce a permutation, and a permutation of eight identical lines is invisible. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the sixth declared stdout line from `Ada@7` to `Ada@8` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 86c5363e18c4d75345d5b50d9b2d2d997a2364a58ad6810ec692c409556036cb before and after, that being this file's digest at the moment the mutation ran — i.e. this text without this parenthetical, which the house convention appends afterwards and which is why the digest of the shipped file is necessarily different). The sixth line is chosen because it is the merge spelling, the only one whose output depends on a SECOND capability actually reaching the body.
